claims.claim: Theophilus of Alexandria was Patriarch of Alexandria from 385 to 412.
Theophilus succeeded Timotheus as bishop of Alexandria in the last week of July 385.
Very little survives of Theophilus' writings, and much of what does survive is either incomplete or of questionable authenticity.
The surviving fragments of Theophilus' writings are scattered in Greek, Latin, Coptic, Armenian, Syriac, and Arabic.
Theophilus' name is connected with three important historical events: the decay of paganism in Egypt, the Origenistic controversy, and the deposition and banishment of St. John Chrysostom.
About 390 Theophilus deprived the pagans of Alexandria of a temple, and with Theophilus at their head, the Christians retaliated by destroying the celebrated temple of Serapis.
Theophilus was distinguished for his persecutions of the Origenists.
Theophilus' surviving works include festal letters, homilies, and letters related to the Origenist controversy.
